sampling_model.design: A graph-only draw of \(\ell\sim q\), followed by a weighted random-priority sequential greedy isolated set and balanced complete randomization over its focal units.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, directed graph, and full potential-outcome schedule are fixed; only the design is random.
sampling_model.treatment: For treated focal \(i\), all units in \(D_i\) receive treatment; for control focal \(i\), all units in \(D_i\) receive control; remaining assignments are fixed by the prespecified rule.
sampling_model.overlap: Every priority order under every library rule produces at least two isolated units, so both RDIM arms are nonempty.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Exact risk uses only the known graph and randomization law; the arbitrary-graph fallback uses independent offline design simulations, not field outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 bounds RDIM MSE using degree-distribution discrepancies and reciprocal isolated-arm sizes, and Section 4.2 minimizes a simulated surrogate.
Randomized graph clustering permits resampled exposure probabilities and exact randomized 3-net probability computation is hard on general graphs.
Counting linear extensions is not FPT in cover-graph treewidth unless \(\mathrm{W[1]}=\mathrm{FPT}\), but is FPT in incomparability-graph treewidth.
Counting linear extensions from a width-\(w\) cover-graph decomposition is possible in \(\widetilde O(n^{w+3})\) time using multivariate-polynomial joins.
Random sequential adsorption yields occupancy probabilities on regular and locally tree-like graphs.
Local-limit differential equations compute asymptotic random-greedy independent-set densities for broad graph sequences.
Semidefinite and nonlinear programming compute minimax optimal designs for semidefinite-representable criteria on discretized design spaces.
Matrix Bernstein bounds the maximum eigenvalue of a sum of independent centered bounded self-adjoint matrices.
Worst-case cluster-design MSE is optimized through a penalized min-cut and semidefinite relaxation under network interference.
The Conflict Graph Design attains a finite-sample variance bound of order \(\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) for a modified Horvitz--Thompson estimator.

Section 6 and Appendix A, especially Lemma A.10, analyze the unrestricted joint design-and-estimator minimax problem through an implicit functional involving distributions over maximal independent sets.

body.tldr: Weighted random isolation makes full-neighborhood treatment and control observable on a random independent set, but its restricted difference in means has random denominators and can be biased for the finite-population total effect. The core reduction writes this error as a \(2n\)-coordinate linear form and shows that every exact risk entry is determined by one- and two-marked isolated-count polynomials. The tier-bearing question is whether those polynomials admit an output-sensitive fixed-parameter algorithm in conflict-graph treewidth, yielding an explicit-runtime certified minimax mixture, or whether a required marked coefficient is parameterized-hard. A complete exact forest oracle supplies the positive base case. Exact rational matrices feed a standard finite-library ellipsoidal SDP consequence, while independent offline simulations give an operator-norm certificate on arbitrary graphs.

project_justification.gap: AWRI selects priority weights using an MSE surrogate, randomized graph clustering resorts to exposure-probability resampling on unrestricted graphs, and order-counting theory warns that bounded treewidth does not automatically make priority integration fixed-parameter tractable. The closest unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax analysis leaves its maximal-independent-set functional implicit and does not compute the prespecified WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count risk.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is an exact, output-sensitive oracle for the marked isolated-count moments that determine dense RDIM risk, together with a positive-versus-hard separator frontier and an explicit certified-mixture guarantee on the positive branch.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact marked-moment reduction, establishes rational output and a complete forest base case, and asks for either fixed-parameter separator compression or parameter-preserving hardness. On the positive branch, standard semidefinite optimization converts the exact oracle into an exactly certified WRI mixture with a stated runtime; arbitrary graphs retain a simulation fallback.

body.related_work: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li supply the WRI/RDIM setup, directed full-neighborhood motivation, and surrogate-based weight-selection arc that informs the present setup. Ugander and Yin show how offline random graph-design draws can estimate otherwise intractable probabilities and establish a neighboring general-graph hardness boundary. Eiben, Ganian, Kangas, and Ordyniak show that the relevant order-counting intuition is representation-sensitive: cover-graph treewidth does not yield FPT linear-extension counting, whereas incomparability-treewidth does. Kangas, Koivisto, and Salonen handle cover-treewidth joins by multivariate polynomial multiplication with an exponent depending on width, the closest algorithmic analogue to the direct WRI messages. Pippenger and Krivelevich, Mészáros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman analyze random greedy occupancy and asymptotic size, but not exact weighted marked count distributions. Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong provide the standard minimax semidefinite-design machinery used only after causal risk matrices are available. Viviano et al. optimize cluster partitions under worst-case network MSE, while Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw study a different conflict-graph estimator. Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje are the closest unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax and maximal-independent-set comparator: version 1, Section 6 and Appendix A, especially Lemma A.10, develops an implicit unrestricted functional, whereas the present theorem-level question concerns exact computation of a prespecified WRI/RDIM marked reciprocal-count functional and a certified restricted-library mixture. The unrestricted comparator informs scope; it is not claimed to be tightened or reproduced.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The direct nice-tree-decomposition construction stores piecewise multivariate priority polynomials with \(\binom{nb+w}{w}\) coefficients and therefore proves only XP complexity. Finite checks on widths two and three can falsify a proposed invariant but cannot establish FPT. The field-level contribution requires either a representation closed under exact joins and forget integrations with exponent independent of \(w\), followed by the stated certified-mixture runtime, or a parameter-preserving hardness reduction for a required marked coefficient. The standard finite-SDP consequence, the exact forest oracle, and matrix concentration do not by themselves settle this separator boundary.
body.honest_scope: The exact linear-risk reduction, rational-output bound, forest recurrence, standard finite-SDP consequence, and matrix-concentration fallback are all posed for proof, not treated as established by the presolve draft. The separator-compression versus parameterized-hardness dichotomy remains the genuine open content, and neither branch is asserted as proved. The finite-library minimax result concerns a prespecified WRI/RDIM oracle and does not claim equality with the unrestricted joint design-and-estimator minimax functional of Kandiros, Harshaw, and Sävje. Under an empty conflict graph the construction reduces to balanced complete randomization, providing the required classical sanity check.
